partial_order.label: Topological Sorting Bypass via Partial Orders

edges.description: Distance entropy determines optimal interval granularity in recursive decomposition. Low-entropy distance distributions yield shallow recursion trees.
Pivot sampling reveals the structure of the partial order without computing it explicitly. Pivots are antichains in the distance partial order.
Hot edges (far from equilibrium) need immediate processing; cold edges can be deferred. Temperature schedule = batch processing schedule.
Recursive interval decomposition on distances mirrors recursive separator decomposition on graph structure. Both create a tree of subproblems.
Spectral sparsification via random sampling and pivot-based distance sampling both use random sampling to preserve structural properties with fewer elements.
Both reduce per-operation overhead: bit-parallelism by packing, lazy evaluation by batching. Combined: batch updates and process batches with bit-parallel operations.
The amortized potential function IS the thermodynamic free energy. Minimizing total work = minimizing free energy of the algorithm's state space.
Entropy-coded distances use fewer bits, enabling more distances per word in bit-parallel operations.
Sampled pivots define the interval boundaries for recursive decomposition. This is the core mechanism of Duan et al. 2023/2025.
The partial order on vertices by distance defines a natural potential function. Width of partial order bounds the potential increase per operation.

bridge_chains.description: Information-theoretic analysis of distance distributions -> optimal interval sizes for recursive decomposition -> sampling rate for pivots. This chain connects compression theory to concrete algorithm parameters.
bridge_chains.actionable_insight: Measure the empirical entropy of distance distributions on test graphs. If H(D) << log n, use finer intervals (more pivots) to exploit the structure.

bridge_chains.description: Thermodynamic temperature schedule -> deferred batch processing -> bit-parallel batch execution. This chain suggests a concrete algorithm: maintain a temperature that determines batch size, process batches with word-level parallelism.
bridge_chains.actionable_insight: Design a 'cooling schedule' for SSSP: initially process edges in large batches with coarse distance granularity, progressively refine to smaller batches with finer granularity.

bridge_chains.description: Partial order width analysis -> potential function bounding PQ operations -> recursive decomposition depth. This chain shows that graphs with narrow distance partial orders enable shallow recursion with few total PQ operations.
bridge_chains.actionable_insight: For the novel algorithm, design the potential function to track partial order width, not just heap size. This could yield tighter amortized bounds.
